transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Rivera (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Head of ML - BlueBranch), Carlos Ruiz (Platform Eng), Ava Thompson (CTO)
---
Summary: Short scoping for a 2-week POC focusing on latency SLOs (TTFT) vs per-token TPOT measurement, workload slices, measurement plan and ownership. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, heavy emphasis on p99 behaviour under bursty traffic and cold cache.
Topics: SLO definitions, traffic decomposition, benchmark measurement plan, sample sizes, acceptance criteria, timeline and owners, security/cert questions.
Action items (recap later in call).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sasha: Hey everyone thanks for joining, apologies for the slight delay, we had a calendar glitch. Quick roll call?
[00:18] Priya: Priya here, thanks. Carlos here. Ava here.
[00:23] Sasha: Awesome. Daniel, do a quick intro on the SE side and what we'll cover?
[00:28] Daniel: Yeah, hi all, Daniel Cho, Redwood SE. Today we want to align on what you need to call a successful pilot: which latency metrics matter (TTFT vs TPOT), the traffic slices we should replicate, how to measure p95/p99, and who owns what. I'll sketch a measurement plan and we can adapt.
[00:50] Ava: High level goal from us — shipping a chat assistant that feels snappy. We care a lot about first token latency for user perceived responsiveness, but also overall cost. So tradeoffs matter.
[01:05] Priya: Right and our internal SLAs talk about sub-200ms for "first response" for most queries, but that's on our optimized infra. We need to see realistic numbers on real models.
[01:20] Daniel: Noted, and to be clear we use TTFT to mean time-to-first-token, i know sometimes folks say TFTT but same idea. TPOT we use for total per-token or total token processing time — basically per-token throughput aggregated across response length.
[01:38] Carlos: One quick infra note: our public-facing endpoints sit behind a CDN and a few load balancers, we'll either replay traffic through Redwood hosted endpoints or run tests inside our VPC for private pilot. We'll confirm egress and auth.
[01:52] Sasha: Great. Ok let's talk SLO framing. Quick question — do you want us to propose both TTFT p95/p99 and a TPOT p95/p99? or pick one as the primary?
[02:05] Priya: Both please. Ops cares about tail latency (p99) and product cares more about p95 for user experience. If both meet thresholds that'd be ideal.
[02:16] Daniel: Cool. Proposal: define three traffic slices — short (<=32 tokens), medium (33-256), long (>256). For each slice measure: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95/p99, and tokens-per-second throughput under steady-state. Also capture cold vs warm cache cases.
[02:40] Ava: That segmentation makes sense. Also we need a burst test for tail behavior — like 10x normal qps for 30s bursts.
[02:49] Sasha: Yeah we'll include ramp and burst. Now numbers, early proposal from Redwood: TTFT p95 target 150 ms for short, 250 ms p95 for medium, p99 we propose 350 ms short and 600 ms medium. TPOT p95 goals we suggested 60 ms/token short, 120 ms/token medium — these are rough depending on model.
[03:14] Priya: Hmm p95 150 ms on short seems aggressive — our current infra sits around 120ms p95 but that's on a smaller model and local cache, plus we do a lot of pre-warming. Are these with KV cache on?
[03:26] Daniel: Good point — all targets will specify cache state. We'll run both warm (KV/prefix cached) and cold runs. The numbers I gave assume warm KV cache and optimized kernels. Cold p95 will be significantly higher — we should capture both for acceptance.
[03:41] Carlos: Also clarify measurement envelope — do these times include network RTT from end user to endpoint + model execution? We need end-to-end numbers else product SLAs are meaningless.
[03:52] Sasha: We'll measure end-to-end from a synthetic client located in your region (we'll run from an env in the same cloud region as your prod). For private VPC testing we'll measure from your internal test agents.
[04:05] Ava: How about p99 sample size? We need statistical confidence.
[04:11] Daniel: For p99 we recommend at least 10k samples per slice for steady-state to have stable tail estimates; for p95 2k samples per slice is usually fine. For burst tests we'll do repeated bursts to gather enough tail samples.
[04:28] Priya: 10k per slice might be heavy but doable if we spread it. Timing?
[04:33] Sasha: Proposed pilot timeline: Week 0 (this week) — finalize slices and runbook; Week 1 — run synthetic benchmark runs (steady-state 2h per configuration, plus 3x 30m burst tests); Week 2 — analyze results, compare to acceptance criteria, demo findings and next-phase recommendation. So ~2 weeks end-to-end.
[04:54] Carlos: For the steady-state 2h, is that per model variant? We plan to test two model sizes and quantization configs.
[05:01] Daniel: Yes per variant. We'll schedule runs sequentially and can parallelize where capacity allows. We'll also capture resource utilization (GPU, memory, kernel stalls) to explain anomalies.
[05:15] Priya: On measurement method — do you provide the harness or we run locally?
[05:20] Sasha: Redwood provides a benchmark harness + load generator (we'll share the script). You can run from your infra or we can run from Redwood-hosted infra against a private endpoint (tunnel/secure). We'll include instructions for warm/cold cache setup.
[05:36] Ava: Security constraints: we need SOC2 docs and SAML SSO for the console, and KMS integration for keys if we do private. Also audit logs access for the pilot.
[05:49] Sasha: Yes, we'll attach our SOC2 and network diagrams. SAML SSO and KMS are supported; for the pilot we'll default to short-lived keys and provide audit log extracts.
[06:00] Carlos: Ok the trickier piece is traffic sampling. We'll provide anonymized traces but we need Redwood's help to translate to replay scripts.
[06:08] Daniel: We can parse traces and produce a sampling plan. We'll ask for 7 days of traffic and then pick representative 1-hour windows across different load shapes: baseline, morning spike, and post-release burst.
[06:21] Priya: Make sure you preserve request/response length distribution in sampling, especially the long-response tails — those drive TPOT and p99.
[06:29] Daniel: Absolutely. We'll compute histograms and ensure replica slices match your production distribution.
[06:34] Sasha: On acceptance criteria, suggest a pass/fail matrix:
[06:38] Sasha (cont): - Green: TTFT p95 within proposed target and TPOT p95 within target for all slices, p99 within a relaxed multiplier (1.5x)
[06:47] Sasha (cont): - Amber: p95 met but p99 exceeds target by <2x or only one slice misses
[06:54] Sasha (cont): - Red: p95 misses or p99 >2x or systematic failures during burst
[06:59] Priya: Amber is fine but we need documented mitigation steps and runbook for fallback to smaller model or dedicated reserved capacity.
[07:09] Daniel: We'll include runbook suggestions: model fallback, request-level degrade (lower top_p), and routing to a warmed small model.
[07:16] Carlos: One more ask: on telemetry, we want per-token cost estimates and token-level latency breakdown (tokenization, network, model).
[07:25] Daniel: We'll output per-request breakdowns and aggregate cost estimates based on your expected tokens per month. We'll include a token-cost calculator in the spreadsheet.
[07:35] Ava: Ok timeline-wise who signs off on success?
[07:38] Priya: I'll be the internal sign-off on accuracy of measurement and product will sign on perceived performance — Ava final signoff.
[07:46] Sasha: Great, we'll capture owners in action items.
[07:50] [brief crosstalk, background noise]
[08:05] Daniel: Couple implementation details — measurement windows should exclude outlier maintenance windows and cadence from our orchestration. Also we should standardize clock sync and use NTP on agents.
[08:16] Carlos: We'll confirm NTP and timezones, yeah.
[08:20] Priya: About p99 cleanup — do you exclude network blips? We need to define outlier rejection rules.
[08:27] Daniel: We'll define a post-processing policy: drop samples where client RTT > 3x median for that window or where infra maintenance flags present. Everything else included. We'll share the exact script.
[08:38] Priya: Sounds good. Also, can Redwood include a brief comparison vs Anthropic managed endpoints? We want an apples-to-apples baseline.
[08:47] Sasha: We can include a competitor baseline but we need credentials/consent to run or public published numbers. We'll add a high-level table comparing expected tails.
[08:55] Ava: Ok. Anything else?
[08:58] Sasha: Quick note on cost: we'll show cost per 1M tokens for each model/quantization in the spreadsheet. That helps tradeoffs.
[09:06] Priya: Perfect.
[09:10] [longer pause, meeting moves to specific dates]
[09:40] Sasha: Recap / next steps: 1) Sasha sends benchmark template + runbook; 2) Priya/Carlos provide anonymized traces and env constraints; 3) Daniel prepares load script and executes, schedule tests week of July 6; 4) Redwood produces draft results deck week of July 13.
[10:05] Priya: I'll confirm data sharing and internal review. Also will ping Legal for NDA extension if needed.
[10:12] Carlos: I'll check VPC peering options and send network diagram.
[10:18] Ava: I'll allocate budget and ensure exec visibility.
[10:22] Sasha: Thanks all. We'll set a follow-up on July 15 to review results unless earlier.
[10:30] Priya: Thanks, bye.

Notes on measurement plan (post-call summary):
- Traffic slices: short (<=32 tokens), medium (33-256), long (>256)
- Sample sizes: steady-state: 2k samples (p95) and 10k samples (p99) per slice; burst tests: repeated bursts to accumulate ~5k tail samples per burst scenario
- Cache states: run both warm (KV/prefix) and cold (empty KV) for each configuration
- Metrics: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory, kernel stalls, error rate
- Measurement method: end-to-end synthetic client in-region; private VPC agent for private run; clock sync mandatory; outlier rejection rule documented
- Acceptance matrix: green/amber/red as discussed with explicit mitigations for amber
- Timeline: finalize runbook by 2026-07-01, tests week of 2026-07-06, analysis week of 2026-07-13, draft findings 2026-07-15
- Owners: Sasha (overall Redwood owner), Daniel (benchmark engineer), Priya (customer measurement lead), Carlos (network lead), Ava (exec signoff)

Attachments referenced: benchmark_template.xlsx (to be shared), runbook.md (to be shared), network_diagram_scrubbed.pdf (customer will share link)

End of transcript.
